Hi Ella — thanks for the clear note and the invoice. Short answer up front: intermediate bank charges can be deducted depending on the route and billing instruction; we prefer to receive the invoiced amount net, so OUR would be the only way to guarantee no deduction on our side, but many EUR banks do not support OUR or will add additional surcharges.

Full details below (please share with your treasury):

Beneficiary (pay to):
  Redwood Inference, Inc.
  Account: 9876543210
  Bank: Redwood Bank USA, N.A.
  SWIFT/BIC: RBUSUS33XXX
  Address: 210 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103, USA

Suggested intermediary path for EUR->USD via SWIFT:
  Ordering bank (ACME EUR) -> Correspondent/Intermediary Bank (EUR clearing) -> Redwood Bank USA (correspondent) -> Beneficiary account.

Important payment instruction fields (use these EXACT strings in your bank's payment screen when possible):
  - Payment details / Remittance: INV-ACME-20260630 / ACME PO 4559
  - Remitter name: ACME Corp EMEA
  - Beneficiary reference: Redwood Inference - Invoice 20260630

Billing instruction choices and effects:
  - OUR: Sender pays all fees (ordering bank + any correspondent fees) -> Redwood should receive full invoice amount. Note: some EUR banks block or surcharge OUR; please confirm with your bank.
  - SHA: Sender pays their bank's outgoing fee; beneficiary receives amount minus any correspondent/intermediary fees that are levied en route. This is the most common default.
  - BEN: Beneficiary pays all fees (not recommended).

Typical intermediary fees: USD correspondent fees are commonly in the $15–$50 range depending on networks used and banks involved. If ACME sends SHA, it's likely we'll see a shortfall of ~€13–€47 after conversion, depending on FX and fee billing.

Alternatives to avoid deductions:
  1) Request YOUR treasury to initiate payment as OUR (preferred if full-net receipt is required).
  2) Invoice in USD and pay directly to the USD account (avoids upstream EUR->USD conversion at the sender bank but requires ACME to accept USD invoice).
  3) Send as SHA and we can invoice a small reconciliation charge if a shortfall is received (this requires internal approval).

I attached our formal wire instruction PDF. If you decide to proceed as OUR, confirm and we will copy finance to verify acceptance for this account.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call with your treasury to walk through their payment UI if helpful.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference

--
